record.paper_title: Operations Research challenges in forestry: 33 open problems
record.original_question: Hierarchical planning typically aggregates products, stands, or spatial detail at higher levels and disaggregates them later, but the well-understood LP aggregation theory breaks down when road-building or spatial decisions introduce integer variables. The open question is how to develop aggregation and disaggregation methods for hierarchical planning when the underlying models are mixed-integer programs.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 31 How can we develop aggregation and disaggregation processes when MIP models are used in hierarchical planning?

artifact.status_search_result: The question of systematic aggregation/disaggregation for MIP-based hierarchical planning remains open. While LP aggregation theory is well developed and partial results exist (e.g., aggregation/disaggregation in integer programming by Rogers et al., iterative aggregation for network design problems), no general theory provides feasibility and provable optimality bounds for hierarchical MIP planning with spatial/road-building integer decisions. Recent forestry OR literature continues to flag incoherent disaggregation between strategic and tactical MIP levels as an unresolved methodological challenge.

status_evidence.title: Aggregation and Disaggregation in Integer Programming Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational work on aggregation in integer programming, but does not yield a general hierarchical planning framework.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results exist for aggregation in integer programming.

status_evidence.title: Solving network design problems via iterative aggregation
status_evidence.snippet: Iterative aggregation methods for MIP network design — problem-specific rather than a general hierarchical theory.
status_evidence.claim: Special-case techniques exist but no general MIP hierarchical aggregation theory.

status_evidence.title: On the risk of systematic drift under incoherent hierarchical forest management planning
status_evidence.snippet: Disaggregation between strategic and tactical forest MIPs can be incoherent in practice.
status_evidence.claim: Hierarchical MIP disaggregation in forestry remains methodologically unresolved.
